title: Projectile Target Challenge: Pick Angle and Speed
description: A launcher sits at the left end of a flat 70 m field with marks every 10 m. A red target zone with a flag sits down the field. Set the launch angle (the barrel tilts) and speed, then press Launch: the ball flies its arc with a trail, and your previous arc stays as a faded line. Readouts give landing distance, miss, flight time, highest point, launches used and targets hit. Hit targets at 30 m, 45 m and 18 m within 10 launches.

game.objective: Hit three targets (30 m, 45 m, then 18 m) by landing within 1.5 m of each centre, using no more than 10 launches.
game.hint: With the same speed, angles that add up to 90° (like 30° and 60°) land at the same distance, and 45° goes farthest. Doubling the speed makes the shot go four times as far.

assumptions: Simplified simulation: no air resistance, and the ball starts at ground level on flat ground.
Gravity is 9.8 m/s² straight down. Sideways speed stays constant; only vertical speed changes.
Each flight point is computed exactly from the projectile formulas, so landing distance = speed² × sin(2 × angle) ÷ 9.8 (at most about 64 m at 25 m/s and 45°).
The ball is treated as a point (drawn enlarged so it is visible); a hit is a landing within 1.5 m of the target centre, both edges counted.
Every flight is shown over 2 seconds of screen time, so screen time does not match the flight-time readout. Reset replays the same targets and clears score and trails.
